neighbours.label: Someone losing, or being at risk of losing, their job or place: being fired, cut, released, not retained or 'shown the door'
fire: One more bad week and the manager could lose his job.
The airline cut costs, and two thousand pilots lost their jobs.
After the heavy defeat, the club sacked its coach on Sunday.
The board voted not to keep the chairman after the scandal.
The rookie kept missing tackles, and the team decided to cut him.
That embarrassing interview almost cost the host her job.
If the merger goes ahead, many clerks will be laid off.
The striker has not scored all year, and the club might release him in January.
quiet: One more good week and the manager could win the award.
The airline grew fast, and two thousand pilots joined the company.
After the big victory, the club praised its coach on Sunday.
The board voted to thank the chairman after the meeting.
The rookie kept making tackles, and the team decided to start him.
That charming interview made the host famous overnight.
If the merger goes ahead, many clerks will move to a new office.
The striker has scored all year, and the club might praise him in January.

notes: Probe: 'shown the door' 1.29, 'release him' 1.06, 'cost the coach his job' 0.82, 'not to retain' 0.77, 'lose their jobs' 0.65, 'fired its manager' 0.54, 'keep her job' 0.22; neutral 'started his job' 0.06 and 'described her job' 0.02. Meaning without the word 'job' fires, so this is a context label.
